body:
DS41's drafter rebuilds metadata eagerly before a FULL query-graph replay. This experiment carries [vLLM PR 3](https://github.com/christopherowen/vllm/pull/3): run the existing integer metadata kernel inside the query graph, preserving the eager fallback guards and native arithmetic.

Two fresh GPU boots now prove a component improvement. At 8 requests/8K, one metadata group and an integer consumer:

| Mean time per operation | Boot 1 | Boot 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Eager host builder | 218.154 µs | 225.644 µs |
| Metadata inside query graph | 5.128 µs | 5.096 µs |
| Saving, paired 95% interval | 213.026 µs [212.471, 213.585] | 220.547 µs [220.016, 221.092] |

The selected placement also beat direct-kernel and separate-graph alternatives. Across 16 cases, isolated savings were 210–228 µs. However, with about 775 µs of GPU work queued ahead, the exposed saving was only **2.940 µs [2.578, 3.308] and 2.663 µs [2.418, 2.905]**. The large isolated reduction is not a serving-speed prediction. No model weights or serving workload ran.

`experiments/2026-11-05-drafter-metadata-replay/micro-results.md` records all comparisons and limitations. `runs/micro-20261106/` preserves raw paired samples, logs, exact commands, source hashes, memory and thermals. Each boot used 24 paired trials, fresh caches and a two-CPU/8-GiB limit; no released build was benchmarked.

Validation:

- Three GPU regression cases and 192 exact metadata/consumer comparisons passed per boot, including padding and slot reuse, with compilation frozen before capture.
- Fresh application of all 573 patches reproduced source `a2b0ea500dc5022e23c4d6fc667254a806c984dc`, tree `e11945731049bb810c69644d91b0740fb3ca3680`.
- Candidate doctor, whitespace checks, 35 host graph tests and all applicable source pre-commit hooks pass.
- Deployment repository suite: 755 tests, 5 skipped, OK. Its synthetic benchmark fixtures are not performance evidence.
- Container peak was about 1.11 GiB, including compilation and all alternative graphs. Incremental serving memory is not yet measured.

Keep draft and launch disabled pending candidate image build, rank agreement, target verification/sampling, cancellation/streaming, startup/deadlock checks and two candidate serving boots against compatible saved references. No serving gain is established. The owner-authorized Spaceport screen respected reservations and yielded between boots. No serving cluster, promoted configuration or immutable baseline was changed.


Acceptance: the owner accepts correctness improvements with preserved performance; a speedup is not mandatory for that route. Current claims are separated explicitly in `results.json`, `decision.md` and the qualification plan: integer equivalence passed; a component speedup was measured; no pre-existing correctness defect is demonstrated; serving latency, throughput and memory preservation remain unmeasured. A correctness repair requires an affected-path old-fails/new-passes reproducer. Performance preservation requires bounds excluding a meaningful regression within the existing comparison/noise limits; an interval merely containing zero is inconclusive. Optional tuning must not block an independently evidenced correctness repair.


Full pinned build preparation and `bin/spark build check` now pass on Spaceport for source `a2b0ea500dc5022e23c4d6fc667254a806c984dc`. All source trees, submodules, locked wheel hashes and exported contexts were verified. The first preparation attempt lacked pip; its failure and the successful retry in a separate pip 25.2 environment are archived with `inputs.json` under `runs/build-20261106/` in the deployment experiment. This is CPU preparation, not an image build or additional GPU/serving validation.
title: Measure DSpark drafter metadata replay and overlap limits
